Technical details of multiple security fixes included in Apple's operating system updates today show that AI tools are rapidly integrating into vulnerability research work. The following are the relevant details.

AI Tools Credited in Apple System Updates

Apple earlier released the following updates:

  • iOS 26.6
  • iPadOS 26.6
  • macOS Tahoe 26.6
  • macOS Sequoia 15.7.8
  • macOS Sonoma 14.8.8
  • tvOS 26.6
  • visionOS 26.6
  • watchOS 26.6

Following the release of the updates, Apple immediately updated its security release page, providing detailed information on multiple fixed issues, including the affected components and devices, potential impact, Apple's fix methods, and the list of credited researchers.

One notable detail in today's documentation is its considerable length, especially considering that Apple released the 26.5.2 update less than a month ago, stating that it already included fixes originally scheduled for the 26.6 release cycle.

Another point worth noting is that Anthropic researchers and Claude were credited for fixes related to WebKit, WebKit Storage, and WebDAV, some of which were jointly completed with researchers from Calif.io.

The research team stated as early as May this year that they used Anthropic's Mythos Preview model to build a working macOS kernel memory corruption exploit on the M5 chip in just five days.

Calif was credited for multiple kernel security fixes in each operating system update released today, while more than a dozen researchers were also credited for related vulnerabilities, reflecting that multiple teams may have independently reported the same underlying issue.

In fact, Apple also fixed several other kernel vulnerabilities during this release cycle, with a total of 30 independent CVEs listed across all operating system updates today.

It is worth mentioning that Apple has had access to Claude Mythos Preview through Anthropic's Project Glasswing since April this year. Therefore, the number of vulnerabilities discovered internally using Claude may be higher than what is shown in the public credit list.

Finally, Anthropic is not the only AI company appearing in today's update announcement. Apple also credited research work involving OpenAI Codex Security, Z.AI's GLM, and the NVIDIA AI Red Team.

Although some names also appeared in last month's security bulletin, today's updates further prove the rapid development of AI-assisted security research, and also reflect that companies must quickly adjust their update schedules and bug bounty programs to adapt to this new situation.
